title: Base change for a proper morphism, against an open immersion
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient $A=A_{E,n}$ and the scheme-base data of [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and carry that ambient exceptional right adjoint datum. Let $g:Y'\hookrightarrow Y$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Form the Cartesian square [def-pc-fibre-product] with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, $g':X'\hookrightarrow X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], normalize $Rf^\times$ as the right adjoint of $Rf_*$ using the proper compactification $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)$ and the comparisons in the given datum. Then $Rf'_*$ admits the corresponding right adjoint $Rf'^\times$, and for every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the canonical comparison
$$\beta_K:Lg'^*Rf^\times K\longrightarrow Rf'^\times Lg^*K$$
is an isomorphism. To specify its normalization, write $\Gamma:g_!Rf'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*g'_!$ for the derived proper/open map induced on K-injective representatives by the sheaf map [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison]. The comparison $\beta_K$ is the $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$ transpose of the $g_!\dashv g^*$ transpose of
$$g_!Rf'_*g'^*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{\Gamma}Rf_*g'_!g'^*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}}Rf_*Rf^\times K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_f}K.$$
All open pullbacks here are exact, so $Lg^*=g^*$ and $Lg'^*=g'^*$.

Independently of this optional ambient datum, let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ with the coefficients of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], let $f$ be proper and $g$ an open immersion as above. For every bounded-below complex $K$ of etale origin [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], the analogous canonical comparison for the relative exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is an isomorphism:
$$g'^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'^!g^*K.$$
Here the relative adjunction is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; no existence of the unrestricted pro-etale ambient datum is inferred from this clause [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge].

proof.text:
Let $c=(j,p)$ be the distinguished compactification of the ambient datum and $c_0$ its FullCD bound. Since $f$ is proper and $p$ is separated, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $j:X\to\overline X$ proper. Thus $j$ is a refinement $(\operatorname{id}_X,f)\to(j,p)$ in [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The comparisons and their unit/counit equations in [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] identify the proper normalization $Rf_*$ with $Rp_*j_!$ and the given right adjoint with $Rf^\times$. For a module sheaf $F$, exactness of $j_!$ [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] and clause 1 of [def-weil-full-cohomological-dimension] give
$$R^qf_*F=\mathcal H^q(Rp_*(j_!F[0]))=0\quad(q>c_0).$$
This bound applies to every pro-etale module sheaf, since FullCD in the assumed datum has exactly that quantifier.

source.place: Step 2 repaired: the conditional finite-CD input at the proper normalization

proof.text: Properness is stable under base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], so $f'$ is proper; [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change] makes $g'$ open. Apply [lem-exc-proetale-proper-open-sheaf-comparison] to $(p,r,i,k)=(f,f',g,g')$ to obtain its specified sheaf isomorphism $\gamma:g_!f'_*\xrightarrow{\sim}f_*g'_!$. In particular the map used is the open-adjunction transpose of restriction, not an arbitrarily chosen isomorphism of the two sheaves.

source.place: Steps 3–4 repaired: the pro-etale degree-zero support comparison

proof.text: Step 1 gives the all-sheaf bound required by [lem-exc-proetale-finite-cd-proper-open-interchange]. Apply that lemma to $(p,r,i,k)=(f,f',g,g')$ and the specified sheaf comparison from Step 2. It supplies the natural isomorphism $\Gamma_M:g_!Rf'_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*g'_!M$ on all unbounded inputs, with exactly the K-injective representative required in the statement. Its normalization is $\lambda_M\circ g^*\Gamma_M=1$, where [lem-exc-proetale-derived-open-restriction] defines $\lambda:g^*Rf_*g'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*$. The latter restriction isomorphism is available without the bound or any exceptional adjoint datum, as required later for the independent clause.

source.place: Retained Step 3: extracted derivation and independent restriction, with the all-sheaf hypothesis supplied by Step 1

proof.text:
For $M\in D(X'_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, the open adjunctions [prop-exc-open-adjoint], the given proper adjunction [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint], and $\Gamma$ yield natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,g'^*Rf^\times K)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X}(g'_!M,Rf^\times K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(Rf_*g'_!M,K)\\
&\xrightarrow{t\mapsto t\circ\Gamma_M}\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(g_!Rf'_*M,K)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,g^*K).
\end{aligned}$$
These four bijections fix both the direction and normalization of the comparison.

Supply the right adjoint for $f'$ rather than assuming ambient data for it. Open localization [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] gives $g^*g_*N\cong N$ on module sheaves: after restriction to $Q\to Y'$, $(Y'\times_YQ)=Q$, with identical restriction maps and module actions. Choose a K-injective resolution using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Then [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] computes $Rg_*N$ by $g_*J$, so exact $g^*$ gives $g^*Rg_*N\cong N$ degreewise. Set $H=g'^*Rf^\times Rg_*$. Step 4 at $K=Rg_*N$, followed by this counit, gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,HN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,N).$$
Use [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to give $Rf'_*\dashv H$ its specified unit and counit, and choose this $H$ as $Rf'^\times$. This does not assert a FullCD/refinement datum for $f'$ over $S$.

source.place: Step 3 repaired: existence of the restricted right adjoint

proof.text: Compose Step 4 with $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] turns the resulting natural bijection of representable functors into an isomorphism $\beta_K:g'^*Rf^\times K\to Rf'^\times g^*K$: applying the same construction to the inverse bijection gives its inverse. To compute its actual map, evaluate at $M=g'^*Rf^\times K$ and $1_M$. The successive transposes in Step 4 are $\varepsilon_{g'}$, then $\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}$, then precomposition with $\Gamma_M$, and then the $g_!\dashv g^*$ transpose. The final transpose under $Rf'_*\dashv Rf'^\times$ is precisely the normalization in the statement, by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. Naturality of the Hom bijections proves naturality in $K$. Any other choice of right adjoint is identified by the same natural representables and hence has this comparison. This proves the arbitrary-open ambient assertion.

source.place: Step 4: Yoneda and identification of the specified map

proof.text: For the independent finite-field clause, $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field has only the ideals zero and one. The opens $X',Y'$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so $g,g'$ are quasi-compact and then finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. To check finite type over $k$ directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], take a finite affine cover of $Y$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras $B_i$ and finite affine covers of each inverse image in $Y'$ by finitely generated $B_i$-algebras $C_{ij}$. The union of the generators of $B_i$ over $k$ and $C_{ij}$ over $B_i$ generates $C_{ij}$ over $k$. Their finitely many affines cover $Y'$. Do this also for $X'$. Both proper compactifications $(\operatorname{id},f)$ and $(\operatorname{id},f')$ thus have finite-dimensional sources [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]; use dimension bound zero on an empty source. Hence [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] applies to both proper maps.

source.place: Retained Step 7, first paragraph: Noetherian and dimension hypotheses for both proper compactifications

proof.text: Let $M\cong\nu_{X'}^*M_0$ with $M_0\in D^+(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Exactness [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact] permits termwise application of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison], giving the bounded-below etale-origin witness $g'_!M\cong\nu_X^*g'^{\mathrm{et}}_!M_0$. Apply [lem-exc-etale-origin-proper-open-interchange] to this Noetherian Cartesian proper/open square. Its five-arrow composite gives a natural isomorphism $C_M:g_!Rf'_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*g'_!M$, independent of the witness and satisfying $\lambda_M\circ g^*C_M=1$. Hence use $\Gamma_M=C_M$ in the independent clause. When the optional ambient datum holds, Step 3 and this equation identify the two maps by the open-adjunction bijection.

source.place: Retained Step 7: etale-origin extension witness and extracted site-transport normalization

proof.text: Choose $K\cong\nu_Y^*K_0$ with $K_0\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. By [lem-exc-relative-adjoint-open-origin], the objects $B=g'^*Rf^!K$ and $C=Rf'^!g^*K$ have the displayed bounded-below etale-origin witnesses $g'^{\mathrm{et},*}f_{\mathrm{et}}^\times K_0$ and $f'_{\mathrm{et}}^\times g^{\mathrm{et},*}K_0$. Thus both are in the witnessed full category [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], where the following Yoneda calculation is valid.

source.place: Retained Step 8: extracted witness and bounded-below identification

proof.text:
For every witnessed test object $M$ on $X'$, Step 8 supplies a witness for $g'_!M$ and the canonical $\Gamma_M$. The open adjunctions [prop-exc-open-adjoint] and relative adjunctions [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] give natural bijections
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,B)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X}(g'_!M,Rf^!K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(Rf_*g'_!M,K)\\
&\xrightarrow{t\mapsto t\circ\Gamma_M}\operatorname{Hom}_{Y}(g_!Rf'_*M,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{Y'}(Rf'_*M,g^*K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{X'}(M,C).
\end{aligned}$$
Each relative adjunction has a bounded-below etale-origin source and bounded-below target. Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in the full witnessed category gives an isomorphism $B\to C$; use the inverse Hom bijections for its inverse. Evaluate at $M=B$ and $1_B$: the transposes are $\varepsilon_{g'}$, $\varepsilon_f\circ Rf_*\varepsilon_{g'}$, precomposition with $\Gamma_B$, its open transpose, and its relative proper transpose. This is precisely the canonical comparison of the statement, and naturality of the Hom bijections proves naturality in $K$. A sheaf in [def-sf-fullcd-used-class] gives a degree-zero witness, so this includes that coefficient-sheaf case.

source.place: Retained Step 8: relative Hom-adjunction and Yoneda calculation
